method_selection.citation: teammate research (Aditya), independently verified; DeepFM (Guo et al. 2017); censored watch-time modeling (CWM, KDD'24)
method_selection.why: Validation peaks at epoch 8 and declines through epoch 10 while training loss trends downward, indicating late-stage overfitting. With 15 iterations left, the highest-value next step is a disciplined 3–5 matched-seed reproduction of the externally measured composite under identical checkpointing and compute. Its reported singles are strong enough to justify replication, but acceptance should depend on matched-seed deltas rather than the validation-selected 0.606116 close; subsequent iterations can ablate causal history, session context, auxiliary loss, and ensembling.

rejected.reason: This is the highest-priority ablation if the composite reproduces, but testing it first would not establish whether the previously reported composite gain is reproducible under this harness.

It matches the overfit curve and is proven, but it does not address the more valuable unresolved question of whether the externally verified composite transfers; regularization and early checkpointing should remain controlled within the reproduction.
This is a closing method and would add validation-selection freedom before establishing a replicated single-model champion.

expected_delta_basis: The seq-deepfm-composite method card reports independently verified validation primary of 0.6055–0.6061 versus the parent's 0.6018, with partial implementations explicitly measured worse.

hypothesis: Because the parent telemetry is missing and cannot support an overfitting diagnosis, the defensible diagnosis is pointwise-to-ranking metric mismatch; replacing the controlled five-field FM with the literature-paired listwise regime (k=32, lr=3e-4, up to 100 epochs, patience 10) will improve matched-seed validation primary by about 0.0018, with acceptance predeclared at a mean delta of at least 0.002.

summary.diagnosis: learning-curve telemetry missing; low-confidence rare-ID overfit hypothesis

method_selection.citation: Wu et al., Stochastic Shared Embeddings, NeurIPS 2019; adaptive sparse-embedding regularization literature.
method_selection.why: Learning-curve telemetry is unusable, so the diagnosis is low-confidence; however, the sharp regression from the k=32 long-training listwise package on this small sparse-ID dataset is most consistent with excess capacity memorizing rare IDs. Frequency-adaptive embedding regularization is an eligible, untried, atomic test that directly regularizes rare user/item rows without repeating the failed architecture and loss openings. It should be run on the last measured competitive regularized parent with matched seeds and accepted only if the mean paired gain clears 0.002.

rejected.reason: Already present in the prior regularized DeepFM opening and broadly measured as a champion component; repeating it would not identify a new source of gain.
Premature with 13 iterations left and no replicated single-model champion; ensembling now would consume validation-selection budget before component attribution and matched-seed confirmation.
Also a closing move, and its underlying SWA mechanism has been flat on this benchmark; expected gain is below the convergence threshold.

expected_delta_basis: Wu et al., NeurIPS 2019 reports consistent small gains from Stochastic Shared Embeddings, but this method has no measured reference_primary in the journal and therefore warrants a conservative expectation below the 0.002 acceptance threshold.
